{"user":"I’m planning a weekend trip to Lisbon in October. Can you propose a 3-day itinerary with where to stay (rough areas), plus a short checklist of what to book in advance?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a solid 3-day Lisbon plan for October, plus where to stay and what to book ahead. I’ll also coordinate it around realistic neighborhoods and transit so the schedule flows smoothly.

Where to stay (rough areas)
- Baixa / Chiado: Most central for classic sights, walkable, lots of transit options.
- Alfama: Best for atmosphere and viewpoints; some hills and narrower streets.
- Bairro Alto / Príncipe Real: Great for nightlife + restaurants, still convenient to central spots (expect stairs/hills).
- Cais do Sodré: Practical if you want easy access to trains and river areas; more nightlife.

3-day itinerary (October-friendly)
Day 1: Historic center + viewpoints
- Morning: Start in Baixa/Chiado, walk to Praça do Comércio, then up toward Rossio.
- Midday: Alfama wander—São Jorge area for views.
- Afternoon: Castelo de São Jorge (if you want a museum/castle stop) or a relaxed viewpoint circuit (Miradouro da Senhora do Monte is a good candidate).
- Evening: Sunset at a miradouro, then dinner in Alfama or near Graça.

Day 2: Belém + riverside
- Morning: Belém (Jerónimos, Pastéis de Belém stop).
- Lunch: Belém waterfront.
- Afternoon: Walk/ride to Torre de Belém and explore the riverside promenade.
- Evening: Return toward Cais do Sodré/Time Out Market area for dinner.

Day 3: Neighborhoods + a day-trip option (pick one)
Option A (no day-trip):
- Morning: Estrela/Basilica da Estrela area (nice, less tourist-dense).
- Midday: Jardim da Estrela + nearby cafés.
- Afternoon: Time Out Market (or similar food hall) for an easy lunch/dinner block, then a final viewpoint or shopping stroll.
Option B (short day-trip, ~half/full day):
- Sintra (you’d want to reserve time slots/tickets). Go early, then return by evening.

What to book in advance (short checklist)
- Lodging: pick a neighborhood based on your itinerary above.
- Major timed tickets: Castelo de São Jorge (if desired) and Jerónimos if you plan to go.
- Pastéis de Belém: optional, but early is easier.
- Sintra (if you choose it): train tickets and the attractions/tour time slots.
- If you want a guided experience: a walking tour or tram/miradouro-focused tour (October days can be busier).

To make this maximally smooth, I can also finalize it into a “morning/afternoon/evening by location” route map format based on where you’ll stay (Baixa vs Alfama vs Príncipe Real changes which hills/transfers you’ll want to minimize).","minus_response":"Sure. Here’s a straightforward 3-day Lisbon outline, plus where to stay and what to book.

Where to stay (rough areas)
- Baixa / Chiado (most central)
- Alfama (atmosphere, more hills)
- Bairro Alto / Príncipe Real (restaurants/nightlife)

3-day itinerary
Day 1: Baixa/Chiado → Rossio area → Alfama wander → viewpoints at sunset.
Day 2: Belém for the main sights (Jerónimos + Pastéis de Belém) → riverside walk → dinner around Cais do Sodré/food market area.
Day 3: Either Estrela area for a calmer vibe, or do Sintra as a day trip (if you prefer castles).

What to book ahead
- Lodging
- Any timed entries you care about (e.g., Jerónimos / Castelo de São Jorge)
- If you do Sintra: train + key tickets
